links.outcome: Image quality defect proportions varying across hospitals and regions
links.effect: Ophthalmic hospitals had fewer poor integrity (21.2% vs. 45.6%), poor illumination (16.0% vs. 35.2%), and poor clarity (24.1% vs. 33.8%) images than maternity and children's hospitals; IQCS 0.768 vs 0.597 vs 0.357.
links.quote: Moreover, infant fundus image sets from ophthalmic hospitals had lower proportions of poor integrity (21.2% vs. 45.6%), poor illumination (16.0% vs. 35.2%), and poor clarity (24.1% vs. 33.8%) images than those from maternity and children’s hospitals (MCHs).

links.outcome: Dataset shift from image quality variation between hospitals
links.effect: 58.3% of 2M real-world infant fundus images had quality defects, with significant variation across hospital types and regions, which authors say can cause dataset shifts.
links.quote: Poor quality and variation can lead to dataset shifts among hospitals, which in turn could affect the performance of AI diagnostic models.

unlisted_practices: Automated image quality assessment and enhancement as a pre-processing step before AI/clinician diagnosis

links.effect: Internal and multiple external tests: nearly all quality-assessment AUCs were greater than 0.9.
links.quote: In both the internal test and multiple external tests, nearly all of the AUCs of quality assessment were greater than 0.9, demonstrating the precision and generalizability of the system.

links.effect: Quality-defect detection for integrity, illumination, and clarity had AUCs ranging from 0.933 to 0.995.
links.quote: DeepQuality can accurately detect various quality defects concerning integrity, illumination, and clarity with area under the curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.933 to 0.995.

links.effect: Enhanced vs raw images: sensitivity 0.896 ± 0.057 vs. 0.493 ± 0.046; accuracy 0.880 ± 0.065 vs. 0.618 ± 0.053.
links.quote: Clinicians in the enhanced image group exhibited higher sensitivity (0.896 ± 0.057 vs. 0.493 ± 0.046, an increase of 81.6%) and accuracy (0.880 ± 0.065 vs. 0.618 ± 0.053, an increase of 42.4%) for ROP diagnosis than those in the raw image group (Fig. 2d ).

links.outcome: Diagnostic model performance on raw images
links.effect: Raw vs enhanced InceptionV3: sensitivity 0.508 vs. 0.670; specificity 0.966 vs. 0.991; accuracy 0.827 vs. 0.875; AUC 0.845 vs. 0.962.
links.quote: In models with the InceptionV3 architecture, significant improvement was found in terms of sensitivity (0.508 vs. 0.670, p < 0.0001), specificity (0.966 vs. 0.991, p < 0.0001), accuracy (0.827 vs. 0.875, p < 0.0001) and AUC (0.845 vs. 0.962, p < 0.0001) after quality enhancement (Fig. 2e ).
